title: Adaptive prefetch + slotting for asymmetric dialogues
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem statement: Persistent mixed prompt/response length distributions (short system prompts + long multi-turn responses or long user prompts with short completions) cause standard continuous batching to either over-reserve KV and GPU slab memory (wasting capacity) or to trigger frequent KV evictions and memory compaction (increasing p99 latency). This ticket explores an adaptive prefetch + slotting strategy that: 1) classifies incoming requests into asymmetric dialogue buckets by percentiles of prompt and expected response length, 2) reserves variable KV residency budgets per bucket, 3) applies lightweight prefetch of KV pages only for buckets with high likelihood of long continuation, and 4) performs GPU-slab-aware packing at slot allocation time to reduce fragmentation. Goals: reduce p99 latency regressions under mixed workloads, improve KV hit rate for long continuations, and lower memory compaction events while preserving overall throughput.
acceptance_criteria: Under simulated mixed workload (70% short prompts/30% long responses) p99 token generation latency increases by <= 5% compared to baseline with no prefetching
KV cache hit rate for long-turn sessions increases by >= 12% on average
GPU memory compaction events reduced by >= 30% during 1h soak test
End-to-end throughput (tokens/sec) does not decrease by more than 7% at target load
Feature gated behind runtime flag and default disabled; rollout plan with canary and metrics dashboard defined
work_log: 2026-02-18: Initial spike meeting with Runtime and Serving teams; scoped approach and success metrics
2026-02-22: Prototype classifier added to request router that tags 'asymmetric-long-continuation' or 'short-exchange' based on prompt tokens and prompt metadata
2026-02-27: Implemented per-bucket KV residency budget enforcement; local benchmark harness shows decreased eviction churn for long sessions
2026-03-04: Added GPU slab packing heuristic to slot allocator (round-robin across slabs with slack-aware fill); measured fragmentation metric in CI
2026-03-09: End-to-end canary run on staging with mixed traffic replay; observed KV hit improvements but slight p95 latency tail increase under microburst — investigating pacing adjustments
comments: Maya Chen (2026-02-20): PM note — prioritize correctness over aggressive cost savings for first rollout. Need clear rollback criteria.
SRE review (2026-02-25): Suggested adding metric for downstream request queuing to detect backpressure caused by prefetching.
Tomás Delgado (runtime) (2026-03-01): Prototype PR created for bucket tagging logic — https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4598
Design review (2026-03-05): UX/Console team requests per-customer residency telemetry to appear in console tenant dashboard for Dedicated customers.
Liam O'Neill (2026-03-10): Decided to implement hysteresis on KV eviction thresholds and to throttle prefetch during microbursts to avoid p95 regressions
decision_notes: Prefer lightweight request-side tagging (stateless classifier) so we can gate behavior per route/customer without heavy runtime state
Do not alter global default KV eviction policy in first iteration; enforce per-bucket residency within existing eviction system
Introduce a runtime flag 'enable_asymmetric_prefetch' with three modes: off, conservative, aggressive for controlled rollouts
next_steps: Tune conservative prefetch throttle factors and re-run 4x microburst scenarios
Add per-tenant residency budget metrics to Console and expose via /metrics endpoint
Prepare canary rollout plan: 5% traffic -> 20% -> 50% with rollback on p95 or compaction spike
Write automated regression tests for KV hit-rate and GPU compaction events in CI cluster
